newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Military intelligence agents arrested late yesterday afternoon suspected Alex Boncayao Brigade (ABB) Commander Felimon "Popoy" Lagman for the murder of a policeman in 1992. (PHILIPPINE STAR, PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER, MALAYA)

- The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) granted a 50-centavo increase in the minimum fare for public utility buses and jeepneys effective November 14 (MANILA BULLETIN,PHILIPPINE STAR,MANILA STANDARD,MANILA CHRONICLE,MANILA TIMES,MALAYA,BUSINESSWORLD)

- The chairman of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation national organizing committee, Lisandro Abadia, recommeded that November 22 to 26 be declared holidays in Manila, Pasay, Makati, Mandaluyong, Paranaque and the Subic Freeport Zone. (INQUIRER)

- American Ambassador to the Philippines Thomas Hubbard said the U.S. government is confident Philippine authorities can handle security problems that may arise during the APEC Summit. (MALAYA, MANILA CHRONICLE)

- House leaders yesterday abandoned their version of the tax measures on beer and cigarettes and opted to support the Senate version. Speaker Jose de Venecia said the House panel in the bicameral conference committee on the excise tax component of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package will shift to the specific tax formula proposed by Senator Juan Ponce Enrile. (BUSINESS DAILY,MALAYA).

- Around 350 passengers were feared killed in New Delhi, India after a Boeing 747 Saudia airliner collided in mid-air with a Kazakh airlines plane near the Indian Capital, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said. (INQUIRER)

- The Energy Regulatory Board expects an average 30.41 centavos oil price increase by Thursday or Friday as petroleum products in Singapore, the benchmark for domestic prices, continued to soar. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- Ayala Land Inc had been chosen by the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) as its partner to develop a three-hectare prime lot in Quezon City into a mixed-use residential, commercial and hotel complex. (INQUIRER, BUSINESSWORLD)

- The economy is facing another buoyant year in 1997 with inflation projected to dip to a 10-year low of 6.5 percent and the Gross Domestic Product seen to expand by six percent, the research arm of Bankers Trust said in a report. (Manila Times)

- Business groups led by the Federation of Philippine Industries and the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry said prices of basic goods are expected to go up in December as a result of the forthcoming increase in transport fares and oil price hike. (BULLETIN)

- The agriculture sector grew by 4.17 percent during the first three quarters of the year compared to the same period in 1995 due to significant output of unmilled rice, sugarcane, hog and chicken industries. (PHILIPPINE STAR, CHRONICLE, STANDARD)
